The test image shows tomato leaves with a distinctive silvery-white bleached/powdery appearance across the leaf surfaces, with some browning at leaf margins. The overall color is washed out and pale. This strongly suggests Powdery Mildew.

Let me check one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows early-stage Powdery Mildew with discrete white spots. The test image shows a more advanced stage where the white powdery coating has spread to cover most of the leaf surface, giving the characteristic silvery-white bleached appearance. This matches the KB description: "eventually forming a dense white layer of growth that can cover entire leaves."

```json
{"prediction": "Powdery_Mildew", "confidence": 0.75, "reasoning": "The test image shows tomato leaves with a silvery-white bleached appearance covering the leaf surfaces uniformly, consistent with advanced powdery mildew where the white powdery coating has spread across the entire leaf. Some browning at leaf margins and leaves remaining attached to the stem also match the symptom description. The whitish coating distinguishes this from other diseases like leaf mold (which shows olive mold on undersides) or Septoria (discrete small spots)."}
```
